TV is increasingly for old people

I don't think that young people will ever really "trade up". Internet services like Netflix and Hulu are much more convenient and cheap, and they don't require any special devices to use, aside from something that enables them to be used on a TV, like Chromecast, Roku or even a gaming console.

The inertia of massive companies like Comcast makes me think they will just bribe lawmakers to achieve profits.

Perhaps they will force everyone to buy a TV license... you don't hate Big Bird, do you?

I think for a lot of people, the model of channels seem outdated. Programming set to one channel where the content can only be watched at scheduled intervals? When Netflix releases a new show, they drop all of the episodes at once for you to watch at your convenience.

I got free television for a year as part of a promotion. It was only a standard package, but it was at least 50-75 channels, including a few in HD. I understand the marketing angle; they want me to get this free service, fall in love with it, and when the free period expires, pay $50+ a month to continue.

However, the opposite has happened. I'm in my tenth free month and I think I've used it half a dozen times (most of which were the Olympics which I could have watched on CBC.ca instead). Even if television is free, I'm still not interested. I have my PC rigged up to my television and I've become so used to services like Netflix where I can watch exactly what I want, exactly when I want, commercial free!

Commercials are the biggest enjoyment killer for me when it comes to network television. I try to stay in an ad-free bubble as much as possible because I see them as an attack on my psyche. On some channels, the balance between content and advertising is split nearly 50/50. So not only do I feel like I'm volunteering to be propagandized, I can't even get immersed in what I'm watching. Of course, there doesn't seem to be much on these days that's worth watching. There's certainly nothing on TV that I'm willing to sit through commercials to see. Even with DVR, I have to commercial-skip several times for an hour-long block of content and break my immersion in the show.

It seems like a lot of television content is just a vehicle to sell McRibs and Ford F150s. However both Netflix and HBO have shown that people are willing to pay for programming directly. I for one would be happy to get a stand-alone HBO Go subscription if it was fairly priced.

I will openly say that I have seen the only stream sites to watch shows, and the large majority of stuff that appears on there is absolute garbage. Like you have to be working some dead beat job and have nothing going for your life to get hooked on any of the poorly developed options out there. I am sure that entertainment is going to transition to internet base but it's the pirates that will live the ultimate technological glory.

I'm old and I've given up on TV. The bundled model sucks, with the exception of a few shows, the quality of the content continues to drop, and even with time-shifting tech like DVRs, it's still not as convenient as using the internet. I doubt my kids will ever "trade up" to cable.
Same here. Out of 60+ channels, I found myself watching one or two of them. Bundling is simply not working for me.

This tip was buried in a massive backyard chicken thread. Basically there can be tiny mold spores on oats and other grains. Cooking the oats in the microwave in a thin spread (1/16 inch or less on a plate) until just before they turn black and resemble charcoal.

When i started growing meal worms earlier this year, i would get mold problems roughly every 2 weeks, and change the bedding. Since i wanted to collect the castings/droppings, this was a problem for me. However, since i microwaved the oats before using them, I am currently on month 4 without any mold problems. Also i found that the meal worms and darkling beetles eat carrots more than potatoes and apples. This secondary tip also helped out since the carrots do not mold anywhere near as fast as apples and potatoes.
Growing Meal worms, Microwave your bedding material to help prevent mold.
